{{use mdy dates|date=August 2020}}
'''Jennifer McLoud-Mann''' is an [[United States|American]]{{r|reu|sciam}} mathematician known for her 2015 discovery, with [[Casey Mann]] and undergraduate student David Von Derau, of the 15th and last class of [[Convex polygon|convex]] [[pentagon]]s to [[Pentagonal tiling|tile the plane]].{{r|sciam|npr|guardian|huff|quanta}} She is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Washington Bothell]], where she is currently the Vice Dean of Curriculum & Instruction of the School of STEM. Beyond tiling, her research interests include [[knot theory]], [[Tessellation|tiling theory]], and [[combinatorics]].{{r|profile}}<ref>{{cite web |title=Innovation Renaissance 2024 Seattle /Bothell-Jennifer McLoud-Mann |url=https://attend.ieee.org/newera/jennifer-mcloud-mann/ |website=IEEE |access-date=18 July 2025}}</ref>
== Early life and education ==
McLoud-Mann grew up in [[Weleetka, Oklahoma]]. As a member of the [[Cherokee Nation]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gray |first1=Alyssa |title=Dr. Jennifer McLoud-Mann named new dean of UW Bothell's School of STEM |url=https://www.uwb.edu/news/2024/12/13/dr-jennifer-mcloud-mann-named-new-dean-of-uw-bothells-school-of-stem |access-date=29 July 2025 |work=University of Washington Bothell News |date=13 December 2024}}</ref> she participated in the Oklahoma Louis Stokes Alliance for Minority Participation and McNair Scholars at [[East Central University]].<ref name="IndigMath">{{cite web |title=Jennifer McLoud-Mann |url=https://indigenousmathematicians.org/jennifer-mcloud-mann/ |website=Indigenous Mathematicians |access-date=18 July 2025 |ref=IndigMath}}</ref> She graduated from East Central University in 1997 with a B.S. degree in Mathematics. She is the first person in her family to earn a bachelor's degree.<ref name="IndigMath" /> She completed a M.S. in Mathematics at the [[University of Arkansas]] in 1998.{{r|cv}}

McLoud-Mann completed her Ph.D. in 2002 from the [[University of Arkansas]]. Her dissertation in [[commutative algebra]], supervised by Mark Ray Johnson, was titled ''On a Certain Family of Determinantal-Like Ideals''.{{r|cv|mgp}}

== Career ==
Upon completing her doctorate, McLoud-Mann joined the [[University of Texas at Tyler]] faculty. In addition, she was associate dean of arts and sciences from 2009 to 2013.

In 2013, she moved to the [[University of Washington Bothell]] where she chaired the School of STEM's Engineering & Mathematics division for three years. In September 2020, she became the Associate Dean of Curriculum & Instruction for the School of STEM.{{r|profile}}

After two years of research, McLoud-Mann and research co-director [[Casey Mann]] found the 15th kind of pentagon that can tile a plane.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2015-08-19|title=UW Bothell team makes discovery that rocks the math world|url=https://www.bothell-reporter.com/news/uw-bothell-team-makes-discovery-that-rocks-the-math-world/|access-date=2020-09-15|website=Bothell-Kenmore Reporter|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last1=Peralta |first1=Eyder |title=With Discovery, 3 Scientists Chip Away At An Unsolvable Math Problem|url=https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2015/08/14/432015615/with-discovery-3-scientists-chip-away-at-an-unsolvable-math-problem|access-date=2020-09-15|website=NPR.org|date=August 14, 2015 |language=en}}</ref> This discovery was facilitated by undergraduate researcher David Von Derau, who automated an algorithm developed by McLoud-Mann and Mann.<ref name=":0" /> It was the first tile discovery in 30 years.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Mathematicians Discover 15th Pentagon That Can Tile the Plane|url=https://www.sciencespacerobots.com/mathematicians-discover-15th-pentagon-that-82020152|access-date=2020-09-15|website=Science, Space and Robots|language=en}}</ref>

== Awards ==
McLoud-Mann won the Henry L. Alder Award for Distinguished Teaching by a Beginning College or University Mathematics Faculty Member of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 2008.{{r|alder}} In 2016, she was the recipient of the Distinguished Research, Scholarship, and Creative Activity award, which recognizes scholarly or creative achievement exemplifying the research-intensive education environment of the [[University of Washington Bothell]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Distinguished research award to McLoud-Mann|url=https://www.uwb.edu/news/April-2016/drsca|access-date=2020-09-15|website=University of Washington Bothell|date=April 2016 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
She was the first in her family to obtain a college degree.{{r|reu|sciam}} She is married to [[Casey Mann]]. <ref name=":2"/>
